Subject: Re: Private connector — IP permit-table & egress constraints (initial ask)

Jordan / team / Maya —

Thanks — below is the ops-oriented permit-table and guidance for a customer-managed VPC private connector. I've kept it minimal and pragmatic so your infra team can apply it without long review cycles.

1) Minimal egress targets (recommended) - 3 IPs used by Redwood control plane (TLS endpoints):
  * 52.198.12.45  (control-plane-01.redwood-inference.net)
  * 52.198.12.46  (control-plane-02.redwood-inference.net)
  * 52.198.23.10  (control-plane-failover.redwood-inference.net)
  Ports: TCP 443 (TLS) outgoing only.

2) FQDNs (when your firewall supports FQDN rules):
  * control-plane.redwood-inference.net -> resolves to the IPs above (A / ALIAS records)
  * telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net -> TCP 443 (used for buffered telemetry uploads; optional if you block telemetry)

3) DNS and keepalives - Allow outbound UDP/TCP 53 to your configured resolvers; allow ephemeral outbound ports for TCP/443 flows. We recommend enabling DNS caching inside the VPC to reduce egregious DNS volume.

4) Proxying behavior and TLS inspection - We support two deployment modes: direct NAT (we see your source IPs) and customer-managed forward proxy.
  - Direct NAT (recommended): customer NAT preserves source; Redwood will log the source IP for audit. This is the simplest for allowlisting (permit the 3 IPs above to outbound 443).
  - Forward proxy / TLS interception: if your proxy performs TLS termination and re-encryption (active MITM), Redwood requires client TLS SNI header and a preserved Host header. We do not support client certificate authentication via arbitrary proxies. In proxy scenarios we recommend: 
    * Configure proxy to allow CONNECT to control-plane.redwood-inference.net on 443 (passthrough CONNECT).
    * If the proxy rewrites SNI or intercepts TLS, coordinate with us so we can accept the proxy's egress IPs and provide a proxy-fqdn mapping.

5) mTLS & mutual auth - For higher security, we can enable mTLS on the control channel. That requires:
  * Customer to provide an outbound TLS client cert on their NAT/proxy or host (PEM) and a CRL plan.
  * If you enable mTLS we will provide a server-side CA pin to pin in your proxy config. Note this increases operational complexity; only recommended for high-compliance customers.

6) Firewall snippets (example iptables-like egress rule for onprem gateway)
  - allow outbound:
    iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 52.198.12.45 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
    iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 52.198.12.46 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
    iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 52.198.23.10 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
  - drop rest (careful: ensure other critical services are allowed)

7) Audit artifact (proof-of-possession) - Attached is a signed text blob we can host behind control-plane.redwood-inference.net that proves an outbound handshake originated from our endpoints. For your auditors we can also produce a short signed statement with a timestamp and the configured egress IPs.

8) Telemetry and optional endpoints - If you opt to block telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net, note that metrics/telemetry will be buffered and retried; that is supported but reduces observability.

9) Operational notes & rotation - Our control-plane egress IPs are stable but we rotate them rarely for capacity/failover. We publish rotation windows 30 days in advance via the onboarding drive link (see below). For strict allowlist policies we can provide an IP range CIDR that you can permit during onboarding plus a signed rotation schedule.

Attachments included:
- redwood-egress-permit-table-v1.yaml (permits + FQDN mappings + explanation)
- egress-proof-of-possession.txt (signed artifact)

Jordan — happy to jump on a 30-minute ops call with Canopy infra if they want us to walk through NAT/proxy snippets.

Kimberly Park
Senior Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Jordan —

This is excellent, thank you. A few follow-ups from our infra team after reviewing the YAML: 

- Can you confirm whether the 3 control-plane IPs are single-host NAT addresses (i.e., ephemeral behind a load balancer) or if each maps to a set of instances? We ask because our firewall vendor charges per-address rules and we'd like to understand billing impact.
- For proxy passthrough: our proxy currently injects an X-Forwarded-For header and performs TLS inspection for some hosts. If we configure a passthrough rule for control-plane.redwood-inference.net, will your backend reject the connection if X-Forwarded-For is present?
- Finally, could you host the egress-proof-of-possession at a stable HTTPS URL and provide a SHA256 fingerprint? That way our auditors can fetch and verify without special handling.

If it's easier I'd like to schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow with David and Laura's networking team to finalize the ip table. Possible times: 10:00 or 14:00 PT.

Thanks again —
Maya
Security Engineer, Canopy Health
